title: Integrate eval run tags into model version metadata (run IDs, baseline comparisons, guardrail outcomes)
creator: Jada Williams
project: Model metadata schema v1 + automated changelog generation
description:
We need to attach evaluation evidence to model/version metadata so (a) release notes can make bounded, non-overstated claims, (b) support can trace regressions to the exact eval run(s) that justified a promotion, and (c) enterprise/Private customers can audit “why did this change ship?” without us pasting internal dashboards in tickets.

Today: eval runs exist in eval-harness + internal dashboards, but model version metadata only has ad-hoc notes. As a result, we can’t reliably answer “what baseline was used?”, “was it statistically significant?”, “did safety guardrails pass?”, and “what promptsets were included?” during promotions/rollbacks.

This ticket adds a standardized set of fields on model version metadata for eval run IDs + baseline comparison + guardrail outcomes, with clear public/internal boundaries.

Non-goal: implementing the full eval platform, running new evals, or guaranteeing every release note includes numeric metrics. This is about traceability hooks + schema + ingestion patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Model metadata schema v1 supports attaching 1..N eval references to a model version (per deployment availability is handled elsewhere).
Each eval reference includes: eval_run_id (or URL), harness/version, promptset(s) identifier(s), baseline model version, and a normalized outcome summary.
Support can programmatically trace from model version -> eval run(s) in internal tooling (at minimum, via run ID and dashboard link).

Release notes generator can consume eval metadata and produce safe language (e.g., “Quality: improved on Redwood summarization promptset (internal eval evidence available).”), with redaction rules enforced.
Public vs internal separation is explicit and validated in CI (no leaking private prompt content, customer names, or internal dashboard URLs to public artifacts).
Backfill plan documented for a small set of top models used for beta (Hosted + Dedicated), with “unknown/not provided” allowed for older versions.
implementation_notes:
Proposed schema addition (conceptual; exact field names must align with model-metadata-schema-v1.json):

Add a new optional array on model version objects:
- eval_evidence[]

Each entry should be intentionally “reference-like” (IDs + bounded summaries), not a full metric blob.

Required (internal):
- eval_run_id: string (e.g., "eh_2025-10-18_9c1b3a")
- eval_system: string enum ("eval-harness" | "external" | "partner")
- eval_system_version: string (e.g., git SHA or semver)
- executed_at: RFC3339 timestamp
- baseline_model_version: string (e.g., "redwood.llama-3.1-70b-instruct@3.6.1")

Recommended (internal):
- promptset_ids: comma-separated string list (or repeated string field if schema supports arrays)
- dataset_ids: comma-separated string list
- policy_profile_id: string (the guardrails policy used)
- notes_internal: string (freeform, internal only)

Outcome summary:
- outcome: string enum ("pass" | "pass_with_observations" | "fail" | "inconclusive")
- comparison_summary_public: string (short, safe, non-numeric allowed)
- comparison_summary_internal: string (can include limited numeric deltas, but must not include raw prompts or customer-specific data)

Guardrails block (keep minimal; do NOT embed raw examples):
- guardrails_summary_public: string (e.g., "No regressions observed vs baseline on jailbreak refusal suite.")
- guardrails_summary_internal: string (e.g., "Toxicity p95 -0.02 vs baseline on safety-v4; refusal compliance +1.1pp; see dashboard ...")

Linking:
- dashboard_url_internal: string (internal only; must be redacted from public artifacts)
- artifact_uri_internal: string (e.g., s3:// or gs:// pointer for audit; internal only)

Open question: do we want a normalized “significance” flag? Proposed:
- significance: string enum ("not_tested" | "significant" | "not_significant" | "insufficient_power")

NOTE: Because Linear/Confluence has redaction guidance, we should keep fields that may contain sensitive data in explicit *_internal fields to make filtering easy for the changelog generator + docs pipeline.

Validation rules (to implement in schema validation tooling):
- If comparison_summary_public is provided, it must be <= 280 chars and must not contain URLs.
- Any field ending with _internal is excluded from customer-visible release notes and must never render in Console for non-admin roles.
- outcome == "fail" should block “promotion eligible” in rollout policy engine only if policy requires it (policy engine dependency may come later; for now, surface the evidence and let humans decide).
tasks: Align with Quentin Harris on final field names + placement in schema v1 (version-level vs variant-level).
Align with Jonas Weber / Sana Farid on what qualifies as acceptable public summary language vs internal-only metrics.
Update schema + fixtures: add eval_evidence to example model records (at least 2 families + 1 quant profile).
Add CI validation: enforce public/internal restrictions (no internal URLs in public fields; require explicit *_internal for dashboard links).
Control plane/model registry: allow storing/retrieving eval_evidence on model version records (CRUD and migrations if needed).
Changelog generator: map eval evidence to release note categories (Quality/Safety) and template language (non-overstated).
Docs/Console integration: ensure API surfaces expose only public-safe fields to standard users; admin/support can query internal fields via RBAC-gated endpoint.
Backfill: tag eval run IDs for beta models and document process for Release Eng during promotions (runbook snippet).
Add E2E test: verify internal eval fields never appear in public docs artifact or non-admin Console views.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: leaking internal dashboard URLs or raw promptset names that contain customer identifiers. Mitigation: explicit *_internal fields + CI lint + redaction tests + reuse ENG-9825 rules.
Risk: release notes overstate quality improvements. Mitigation: require comparison_summary_public to be editorially constrained (no % unless approved) + style guide compliance.
Risk: eval run IDs are not stable or not globally unique. Mitigation: standardize on eval-harness run ID format; include eval_system + executed_at; optionally include schema_hash.
Risk: partners want richer metrics than we can safely publish. Mitigation: internal summaries can be richer; public summaries remain qualitative unless stats sign-off.
commentary_and_updates:
2025-10-10 (Jada): Added as dependency for changelog generator so we can link “quality evidence” to promotions. Please keep schema additive; older versions can omit eval evidence.

2025-10-14 (Jonas): Recommend a single normalized “outcome” plus optional significance flag. Avoid publishing raw metric values unless we can guarantee significance and consistent promptsets. Public summaries should be qualitative and scoped (name the promptset family, not internal suite IDs).

2025-10-16 (Michael): Drafted schema fields in branch; need Quentin review for naming conventions + where it lives (model_version vs serving_variant). Leaning model_version because evals are run at a specific build + tokenizer/runtime combo.

2025-10-18 (Sana): For anything framed as an improvement, we should store whether it was statistically significant, otherwise release notes should say “no regressions observed” rather than “improved.”

2025-10-21 (Naomi Feldman): Security note: internal artifact URIs are acceptable for audit but must not be exported in public feeds. Add a unit test to ensure docs generator drops *_internal.

2025-10-24 (Michael): In progress. Next: coordinate with changelog generator template mapping so eval evidence produces a consistent “Quality” section without forcing numeric deltas.
